item.title: Reflecting On The Strength Of A Woman Through The Performing Arts
An Introspection on ‘TranscenDance’
item.description: (Image Source: Temple of Fine Arts) To transcend is “to surpass; to go beyond the range or limits”. We all have our own journeys of transcending from one realization to the next. To some of us, transcendence is likened to progress. Reaching a goal at work, learning something new about parenting, doing better at a particular craft, or realizing a new perspective. Regardless of its experience, transcendence lets us move beyond what we know about ourselves and the significance of our experiences.

item.title: Improvization – and all the jazz
item.description: By Krithika Shekhar Have you ever come out of a situation thinking how unlike yourself that was? A reaction of absolute calm, when it might have otherwise riled you up. A quick burst of anger, when on a regular day a few deep breaths might have brought you out unscathed. No matter how much you may rehearse your reaction for a particular situation, there is no assuring how you will finally end up responding. item.title: Practising Perseverance
item.description: by Krithika Shekhar “Again”. A word that can fill an artist’s heart with pride when on stage and at the request of the audience, or fill one with dread in class and under the teacher’s orders. We’ve all grown up listening to the adage “good things come to those who wait”, but nobody ever tells you how much waiting you need to do. So when do you know if you’ve waited enough?
